audit.why: Swain's ranged root/poke and passive soul-heal dominate the lane through 2+ items per packet.levelChart (Swain 6/7 stages); only late-game Monsoon disengage lets Janna claw back, matching content win[6]=Janna.

Level-6 Demonic Ascension drain spike and first-item Liandry's/Rylai's snowball are already recorded in spikes[]; suspectNames flagged 'His Demonic Ascension' but that IS the correct enemyAbilities.R name, so no fix needed there.

audit.whatIsWrong: All seven phases[N].side carry the placeholder 'Skill' and the full-layer .why text for every row is written as if Janna is winning ('your chip is real and your disengage is law', 'Monsoon online — dives on your duo now end...'), but content win[0-5]=Swain, win[6]=Janna, matching packet.levelChart exactly.
audit.why: THE CHART RULE requires side to agree with win[N]; since the why-text also argued the wrong side for six of seven rows, both needed rewriting together in this proposal. win[] itself needed no edit — it already matched the packet.
audit.corrected: Set phases[0-5].side to Swain (why rewritten from content whys[0-5]: root/poke range, passive soul-heal, Q-fan zone control, root-combo punish, Demonic Ascension drain, Liandry's/Rylai's snowball) and phases[6].side to Janna (why rewritten from content whys[6]: Monsoon disengage breaking his channel late).

edits.before: Auto-harass with Tailwind and hold Q — your chip is real and your disengage is law.
edits.after: Swain's Vision of Empire root and Death's Hand poke out-range Zephyr and win level 1.

edits.before: W-poke the contacts; the tornado threat already taxes their engage plans.
edits.after: His passive soul-heal sustains through any trade you try to start at level 2.

edits.before: Full kit: shield the trades, slow the answers, and break the first real engage with Q.
edits.after: His level 3 zone control with Death's Hand's fan pattern keeps you pushed off the wave.

edits.before: Chip and shield the margins — every broken engage is a won trade your carry banks.
edits.after: Through 4-5 his Nevermove-into-combo punishes any all-in you attempt to make.

edits.before: Monsoon online — dives on your duo now end in a healing field they paid for.
edits.after: Demonic Ascension drains you and your ADC at 6, extending his lead further.

edits.before: First item: shields grow and the disengage toolkit compounds.
edits.after: First-item Liandry's snowballs his DoT and slow against you.

edits.before: Late Janna erases engages: tornado the dive, monsoon the collapse, shield the carry through the rest.
edits.after: Only late does Monsoon's disengage let you break his channel and finally claw back the fight.

edits.before: Auto the carry, W the support, shield the answer — chip trades the wind referees.
edits.after: Death's Hand pierces through you to hit the ally behind — angle behind minions so the bolt count doesn't stack on your ADC.

edits.before: Burning Q on poke and meeting the real engage with a shrug — the tornado is the matchup.
edits.after: Nevermove reaches 850 range and the return-wave roots too — shielding into his rotation just banks him a free pull.

edits.before: - Swain Nevermove: matchup-defining — The root that decides — dodge it and the general farms regret. The duo’s tempo bends around it. - Keep Q Howling Gale banked for their best play. - The ultimate is a fight decision, not a habit.
edits.after: - Swain Nevermove (E) is down 12s at rank 1, 10s maxed — that whiff is your engage window. - Demonic Ascension sits at a flat 120s; once he channels it he won't leave willingly. - Bank Howling Gale (14s CD) for the root, not the poke.
